chunks: And whatever is narrated from Dhurayh Al-Muharibi, I have narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Dhurayh ibn Yazid ibn Muhammad Al-Muharibi. And I have also narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Razin, from Dhurayh.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to the narrator's father, often Ibrahim ibn Hashim in this context)
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.ذُرَيْحٍ الْمُحَارِبِيِّ: Dhurayh Al-Muharibi, a prominent companion and narrator
key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ali ibn Ibrahim, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, a well-known companion

ai.seo_question: How is the narration chain for Dhurayh Al-Muharibi verified in Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq meticulously documents the dual transmission chains for Dhurayh Al-Muharibi, a key narrator in the Kufan school, to validate the reliability of his reports within the *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By tracing the isnad through his father, Ali ibn Ibrahim, and other prominent companions like al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, he reinforces the scholarly consensus on the authenticity of these narrations, a critical step in establishing the legal authority of hadiths that lack direct access to the Imams.
